subject: Dark resinous material seeping from a crack in a high rock face. The material where it comes from, seeping out of a crack in rock.

A high mountain ridge of bare grey rock above the tree line. Bare rock above the tree line. The Altai, the Himalaya, the Caucasus. The material comes off faces like these, out of the cracks, in the warm months.
An unpurified lump of dark material with grit and plant fibre still through it. Raw, as it comes off the rock. Grit, sand and plant fibre still through it. This is an ingredient, not a food.

Fine sediment and grit caught on a stretched cloth filter. What comes out on the cloth. Sand, rock dust and plant fibre. Every pass through a finer cloth takes more of this out, and more of the seller's yield with it.
A clear glass of dark golden brown solution with a clean bottom. Fully dissolved. Golden brown at the edge, near black in the body of the glass, and nothing on the bottom.
A cloudy glass with a layer of grey sediment settled on the bottom. The same test, failed. Cloudy water and a layer of grit that slides when you tip the glass. That layer is rock.
A broken lump of dark resin showing a smooth glassy fracture face. A fresh break in cold resin. Smooth and glassy rather than crumbly, near black with a bronze cast where the light catches it.
Warm resin drawn out into a long thread from the bowl of a metal spoon. Warm resin off a warm spoon. It draws into a thread and thins before it parts. Cold, the same piece would snap.
